title: Pesticide levels along a lake food chain
body: A non-degradable pesticide used on farms near a lake was carried into the water by rain. Students later studied illustrative values of its concentration (in parts per million, ppm) along a food chain in the lake. Lake water: 0.00005 ppm. Zooplankton: 0.04 ppm. Small fish: 0.5 ppm. Large fish: 2 ppm. Fish-eating birds: 25 ppm. The farmers used the pesticide only on their crops and never applied it to the birds or fish directly.

title: Disposable cups in trains
body: Many years ago, tea in trains was served in plastic glasses which had to be returned to the vendor. The introduction of disposable cups was welcomed as a step forward for reasons of hygiene, but no one at that time thought much about the impact of throwing away millions of these cups every day. Later, kulhads, which are disposable cups made of clay, were suggested as an alternative. However, a little thought showed that making kulhads on a large scale would result in the loss of the fertile top-soil. Now disposable paper-cups are being used in many places.
